verdict: Caution: lend selectively to integrated, low-leverage Tiruppur cotton spinners with diversified customers; avoid stand-alone yarn units selling to the local dyeing/apparel chain until order flow and GST collections recover.
title: Tiruppur cotton spinning & yarn: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
A cotton spinner buys raw cotton, converts it into yarn on ring frames, and sells to weavers, knitters and integrated fabric/apparel units. Cash is tied in cotton inventory and receivables, so the working-capital cycle — not the spindle count — decides survival. **Cotton procurement efficiency separates the profitable mills from the rest [11].** Because fixed capital and working capital are both heavy, funding needs are high and leverage is the swing factor [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the cotton buying model and the receivable days first; if the unit buys cotton at peak prices on borrowed money, ask why.

## Where value and cash sit now
Peer results show the split clearly. Nitin Spinners reported record quarterly revenue of Rs. 875 crores, up 10.3% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 17.78%, up 376 bps YoY on better yarn realizations [4]. Sportking India's Q1FY26 revenue was Rs. 585.8 crore, down 7.6% YoY, though EBITDA margin improved 40 bps to 12.0% [5]. **Integrated, export-tilted spinners are holding margin; stand-alone yarn is not.** Sutlej's management says integration absorbs raw-material volatility that stand-alone yarn players cannot replicate [7]. So when a proposal lands, check the share of integrated versus merchant yarn sales; if it is mostly merchant yarn, ask for the customer-wise realization trend.

## What has broken locally
Tiruppur's own signals are weak. Tamil Nadu GST collections fell 3.2% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1%, 9.3 pp slower [D]. Local reporting says industry leaders have flagged a slowdown in incoming orders at Tiruppur apparel units [1][2], and dyeing units are in crisis as raw-material prices rise [3]. Bonus payments are under way and expected to close by November 5, with some unionized units paying slightly higher than last year [1][2]. **The local chain — dyeing, apparel, merchant yarn — is where the stress sits, not in the national IIP print of +13.1% YoY for NIC 13 [D].** Note the rating methodology sources [8][9][10][11] are undated or archived; treat them as principles, not current data.

## Where to grow safely
Pursue integrated spinners with in-house fabric or processing, diversified customers and low leverage — CRISIL views a diversified customer base positively because single-customer concentration stretches working capital [11]. Low leverage preserves financial flexibility in a downturn [10]. **Take term debt with tenure matched to the asset, since longer tenure improves coverage [10].** Structure: monthly stock-and-receivable statements, a drawing-power formula on cotton inventory, and a covenant capping total debt to EBITDA. Collect from customer: current order book, customer concentration, and cotton procurement policy.

## Early-warning signs
- Monthly GST returns (monthly): two consecutive months of falling turnover -> freeze enhancement and re-rate the limit. - Cotton inventory days (monthly): rising while realizations fall -> ask for the buying policy and cut drawing power. - Order book from apparel buyers (quarterly): confirmed decline -> shift to integrated, export-tilted names only.
